findings.body: Both requests can observe the same below-limit count and both insert successfully, causing the active device count to exceed the configured limit.
findings.failure_mode: Concurrent admissions violate the configured upper bound.
findings.impact: Both requests can observe the same below-limit count and both insert successfully, causing the active device count to exceed the configured limit.
findings.root_cause: Quota availability is read and acted upon in separate database operations without serialization.
findings.suggested_fix: Perform quota reservation and insertion in one serialized database transaction using an appropriate lock or atomic quota row, and retry or reject a request that loses the race.
findings.title: The count-then-insert quota check is not atomic
findings.trigger: Two distinct anonymous devices are admitted concurrently when the active count is one below the configured limit, including requests handled by different Grafana instances sharing the database.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at database.go:110-117 shows count is read via CountDevices, then compared, then updateDevice or insert is called in separate operations without transaction isolation. Two concurrent requests can both observe count < limit and both successfully insert, exceeding the configured limit. This is a real TOCTOU race condition.

findings.body: The first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI already cached the device before the failed store operation. The retry hits the cache, returns nil without checking the database, and authenticates successfully despite the limit.
findings.failure_mode: A single retry bypasses device-limit enforcement.
findings.impact: The first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI already cached the device before the failed store operation. The retry hits the cache, returns nil without checking the database, and authenticates successfully despite the limit.
findings.root_cause: The patch begins propagating store errors as admission failures while the pre-store cache entry remains committed on those failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Populate the local cache only after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or explicitly remove the cache entry whenever the store operation returns an error.
findings.title: A rejected device is cached and admitted on its next request
findings.trigger: A new device requests anonymous access after the limit is reached, then retries with the same device ID within the local cache's 29-minute TTL.
findings.verifier_reason: impl.go:80-97 shows tagDeviceUI caches the device key at line 87 (SetDefault) BEFORE calling CreateOrUpdateDevice at line 93. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains. The new line 147 returns the error, but on retry the cache hit at line 83-84 returns nil immediately, bypassing the limit check.

raw_findings.body: Grafana's environment override pass has no auth.anonymous.device_limit key to override because the patch does not add it to conf/defaults.ini; the parsed limit remains 0 and anonymous access is left unlimited.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `device_limit = 0` under `[auth.anonymous]` in conf/defaults.ini so the environment override machinery can discover and replace the key.

validated_findings.root_cause: The added integration test covers only the zero-row rejection branch of updateDevice.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: After filling the quota, call CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the original device ID and changed fields, assert success, and verify the stored fields and timestamp were updated; run this path against supported database dialects.
validated_findings.title: The limit test never exercises the successful update-at-capacity path
validated_findings.trigger: The new UPDATE query or its row-count handling regresses on one of the supported database dialects while rejection of unknown devices still works.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: database_test.go:51-69 tests only the rejection case (new device when limit reached). It never tests that an existing device can successfully update when at capacity. The updateDevice function at database.go:73-102 has specific logic for this case that lacks test coverage, which could regress undetected.

validated_findings.body: The supplied abstraction is no longer accepted or used; callers must provision a real database, tests reach into the private anonStore field, and the existing Wire provider/binding becomes stale.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Dependency-injection overrides and isolated service tests are no longer possible through the constructor.
validated_findings.impact: The supplied abstraction is no longer accepted or used; callers must provision a real database, tests reach into the private anonStore field, and the existing Wire provider/binding becomes stale.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch replaces an interface dependency with an internally constructed concrete database store to pass the limit.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep ProvideAnonymousDeviceService dependent on anonstore.AnonStore, and inject configuration into ProvideAnonDBStore by having that provider accept *setting.Cfg or a dedicated typed options value.
validated_findings.title: The service constructor bypasses the existing AnonStore dependency injection
validated_findings.trigger: A test, alternate implementation, or Wire configuration supplies an anonstore.AnonStore implementation to the anonymous-device service.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: While the patch does change the constructor signature from accepting AnonStore interface to db.DB, this is an intentional design change to pass the device limit. The Wire binding at wire.go:374-375 still exists and tests in impl_test.go work with the new signature. This is a style/architecture concern, not a defect causing incorrect behavior.
